original_question: Does every irreducible arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curve in P^4 admit an Artinian reduction that has the strong Lefschetz property?
target_in_paper: Question 3.3 in Section 3 (subheading "Artinian reductions of arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curves"): "Do all irreducible arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curves in P^4 have an Artinian reduction that has the SLP?" ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official question almost verbatim: it keeps the universal quantifier, the hypotheses "irreducible" and "arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay," the ambient space P^4, the existential phrase "admit/have an Artinian reduction," and the target property is the strong Lefschetz property rather than only the weak Lefschetz property. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))
missing_details: To make it fully stand-alone, introduce a base field K and the homogeneous coordinate ring R = K[x0,x1,x2,x3,x4]/I_C of the curve C. The paper does not add any characteristic restriction in Question 3.3, and that omission matters because the neighboring Questions 3.1 and 3.2 explicitly say "provided that the characteristic of the underlying field equals zero" when such a restriction is intended. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Unpack "Artinian reduction": for an ACM curve C in P^4, one should specify that this means quotienting the standard graded coordinate ring R by a linear system of parameters of length 2, say A = R/(theta_1, theta_2), so that A is Artinian. The paper leaves this standard meaning implicit in Question 3.3. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))

Unpack "has the strong Lefschetz property": one should specify that there exists a linear form ell in A_1 such that for every i >= 0 and d >= 0, the multiplication map times ell^d: A_i -> A_{i+d} has maximal rank. The paper uses the abbreviation SLP but does not restate this operator-theoretic definition at Question 3.3 itself. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))

Preserve the existential force of "an Artinian reduction": the paper does not ask for a general Artinian reduction here. This is a real scope condition, especially because Question 3.1 immediately before it explicitly asks about a general Artinian reduction. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2311.03081))

Do not broaden the class of objects: the paper asks only about irreducible ACM curves in P^4, not arbitrary ACM subschemes, not reducible curves, and not curves in P^n for variable n. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))

No extra degree bounds, generator conditions, nilpotency hypotheses beyond Artinianness, or asymptotic phrases such as "for all sufficiently large m" occur in this problem, so a faithful rewrite should not introduce any. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Let K be a field, let C be an irreducible arithmetically Cohen-Macaulay curve in P^4_K, and let R = K[x0,x1,x2,x3,x4]/I_C be its standard graded homogeneous coordinate ring. Does there exist a linear system of parameters theta_1, theta_2 in R_1 such that the Artinian reduction A = R/(theta_1, theta_2) has the strong Lefschetz property; equivalently, does there exist such a reduction A and a linear form ell in A_1 for which every multiplication map times ell^d: A_i -> A_{i+d} has maximal rank for all integers i,d >= 0?
justification: The draft is targeting exactly the paper's Question 3.3, which appears in the Section 3 block on geometric aspects related to Lefschetz properties. The wording of the draft is already essentially the same as the official formulation. The only sharpening needed is to make explicit the standard meanings of "Artinian reduction" and "SLP" so that the question stands alone. It is also important not to alter the scope: unlike Question 3.1, Question 3.3 does not ask for a general Artinian reduction, and unlike Questions 3.1 and 3.2 it does not append a characteristic-zero hypothesis. So the faithful refinement is to keep the problem exactly at irreducible ACM curves in P^4 and to explicate only the standard graded-algebra definitions that the paper leaves implicit. ([ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl](https://ibwu-konferencja.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2.pdf?utm_source=openai))
